subject: GLN pilot: staged release & early-exit safeguards
messages:
From: Jessica Liu <jessica.liu@greenlinehealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@greenlinehealth.com
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Request: early termination flexibility & ramp protections for GLN pilot

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Greenline's exec team is aligned on moving forward with a 6-month pilot, but a couple of items are blocking final sign-off from procurement/legal:

- Early termination language: they want a clean opt-out at 60 days with a reduced financial obligation rather than the full remaining commit.
- Ramp protections: because we'll be starting small and scaling, procurement is asking for explicit downsell protections—i.e., a staged ramp schedule with graduated commit thresholds and a grace period during the first 90 days.

Our priority is to keep the pilot low-risk for Greenline while giving Redwood enough runway to deliver value. Can you share what exceptions/redlines you can accept? If you have a suggested paragraph for the contract that preserves our economics, that would help speed things up.

I've attached the draft SOW and our procurement team's redlines.

Best,
Jessica Liu
Senior Contract Manager
Greenline Health

Attachment: Greenline_SOW_v1.pdf (PDF stub)
Attachment: GLN_redlines_20270301.docx (docx stub)
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jessica Liu <jessica.liu@greenlinehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 11:04:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Request: early termination flexibility & ramp protections for GLN pilot

Jessica — thanks for the clear ask and the redlines. We want Greenline to feel comfortable taking the pilot, so I've sketched two options below that trade commercial certainty for flexibility:

Option A (Customer-first, lower friction):
- 60-day opt-out: Customer may terminate with 30 days notice after 60 days; customer pays pro-rated usage through termination + an early-release credit equal to 25% of remaining committed fees (capped at 3 months).
- Ramp schedule: 3-stage commit (month 1: 25% of pilot commit; month 3: 65%; month 6: 100%). If usage stays below the staged threshold, a downsell protection allows one-time step-down (to next stage) without penalty within the first 90 days.

Option B (Protect Redwood economics):
- 60-day opt-out: Customer may terminate with 30 days notice after 60 days; customer pays pro-rated usage. Early-release fee equals 50% of remaining committed fees.
- Ramp schedule: same stages, but step-downs incur a 20% fee on differential commit for the remainder of the contract.

I've attached a draft clause (wording) and a quick P&L showing the downside for each option. I'm happy to adopt a hybrid if the customer needs more comfort.

Requesting internal review: marissa and rishi — can we approve Option A for pilots <= $75k ARR with a manual exec sign-off for deals above that? If needed I can route to Vivek for final sign-off.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0198

Attachments: pricing_redline_20270301.xlsx (xlsx stub), GLN_proposed_clauses.docx (docx stub)

Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 08:16:00 -08:00
Subject: FWD: Re: Request: early termination flexibility & ramp protections for GLN pilot

Marissa / Rishi — forwarding Greenline's request and my proposed options (below). Key commercials: target pilot ARR $45k, expected usage ramping to full commit by month 6. If we give Option A we lose some downside protection but improve close velocity.

Ask: approval to accept Option A for this pilot with the following constraints:
- Cap early-release credit at 3 months of committed fees, and require an exit survey + opportunity review before credit is issued.
- Limit step-down protection to a single one-time step during the first 90 days; any further reductions revert to standard termination fees.
- Finance to validate the blend impact — I'm estimating a worst-case revenue impact of 18% over 12 months if customer fully exercises opt-out at month 2.

Attachments included: Greenline_SOW_v1.pdf, pricing_redline_20270301.xlsx

Please reply with APPROVE / DENY / NEEDS LEGAL and any edits.

Naomi — thanks for the clear framing. I agree with approving Option A for this specific pilot given the strategic nature of the account and low ARR. Conditions I want documented: 

1) Cap the early-release credit at the greater of (a) 3 months committed fees or (b) $10k — whichever is lower.
2) Require a written exit review (template in Deal Desk folder) that includes usage metrics and success criteria before credit is issued.
3) Legal to sign off on the exact contract language (no one-line swaps).
4) Rishi — finance check required to confirm the 18% worst-case impact number.

I will APPROVE Option A for GLN-2027-042 contingent on legal and finance confirmations. If either flags material issues, escalate to Vivek for emergency exec sign-off.

Adding finance's quick assessment: I reviewed the sketch and ran a conservative scenario. Findings:

- Worst-case realized revenue loss if customer exits at day 75 and receives the 25% credit: ~16% over 12 months (slightly better than Naomi's 18% estimate due to expected upsell velocity).
- Operational risk: increased touch to validate exit survey + manual credit processing — recommend implementing a one-page exit survey and Deal Desk automation to minimize lift.

Given GLN's potential as a reference in vertical, I SUPPORT Marissa's conditional APPROVAL of Option A.

Next steps: Naomi, publish the approved clause (I'll route to Legal) and attach the exit-survey template. I'll coordinate with Finance to add a quick checkbox in billing to flag pilot deals with early-release credit eligibility.

Thanks,
Rishi
